_comment: Injectable rule docs manifest. Drives optional rule file deployment from the settings browser and headless types. Never read by session hooks. Every entry is opt-in — seiri has no required rules.

rules.title: Agent-Legible Code
rules.description: Make invisible wiring, repeated blocks, name traps, and indirection legible at the point where they bite.
rules.grounding: This rule rests on properties every codebase has: code lives in files with names and paths, and symbols are defined and referenced.

rules.title: Code Comments
rules.description: Inline comments are a capped last resort; declarations take the language's documentation form and state the current spec, never history.
rules.grounding: This rule rests on properties every codebase has: the language provides a form for comments, and a comment sits beside the code it describes.

rules.title: Public Contract
rules.description: Keep a module's exports small, named, and enumerable — entry points declare, internals implement.
rules.grounding: This rule rests on a property every codebase with a module system has: a distinction exists between what is public and what is internal.

rules.title: Test Validity
rules.description: A passing test is evidence only if it could have failed — fail first, verify the artifact you changed, curate suites.
rules.grounding: This rule rests on a property every codebase has: a means of verification exists and can be run.

rules.title: Reuse First
rules.description: Search first, compose second, write last — the smallest change that answers the request.
rules.grounding: This rule rests on a property every codebase has: a change is a diff, and it answers a request.

rules.title: Naming
rules.description: Mirror sibling conventions, name one concrete responsibility, and keep grab-bag files out of the tree.
rules.grounding: This rule rests on properties every codebase has: files and symbols have names, and an existing style is already present — whatever it is.

rules.title: Structure
rules.description: Direction-only structure rules: dependencies form a DAG, depth is a toll, cohesion splits and complexity compresses.
rules.grounding: This rule rests on properties every codebase has: files have sizes and paths, and symbols reference one another.

rules.title: Function Boundaries
rules.description: Functions compute from their parameters, effects stay at the edge, and one file exports one function.
rules.grounding: This rule rests on properties every codebase has: functions take inputs and produce outputs, and they live in files with names.

rules.title: Context Efficiency
rules.description: Spend session context deliberately: generated artifacts are search-only, capture once, re-read with a reason.
rules.grounding: This rule rests on a property of every session, not of any codebase: context is finite, and reading spends it.
